questions.question: Why does a coin have value?
options: Because people agreed that it would have value and could be exchanged for things
questions.explanation: A coin has value because people agreed that money would have value and could be exchanged for things we need or want.

questions.question: Chrumko holds a coin in his hand. How can he use it?
options: Nothing can be done with it
He can buy an apple or juice at the store
He can wear it as jewelry
He can use it for heating
questions.explanation: The coin has value, so Chrumko can use it in the store to make purchases - for example, to buy an apple or juice at the checkout.

questions.question: Which of these options are money?
options: Coins, banknotes, and digital money on a card
questions.explanation: Today we can pay with coins, banknotes, or money on a payment card. These are all forms of money in different shapes.

questions.question: What can you buy with money?
options: Food, clothing, toys, and other things we need or want
questions.explanation: Money is used to buy things we need or want - for example, food, clothing, or toys.

questions.question: Why does money exist?
options: It has no reason to exist
questions.explanation: Money exists to make buying things easier. Without money, people would have to trade items, which would be very difficult.

questions.question: Chrumko has an apple for snack but wants a cereal bar. What would be the problem without money?
options: He would need to find someone who wants an apple and has a cereal bar
questions.explanation: Without money, people would have to trade items with each other. That would be very difficult because you'd need to find someone who wants exactly what you have.

questions.question: How is it easier with money?
options: I can buy a cereal bar right away without finding someone who wants exactly an apple
I have to negotiate with more people
questions.explanation: When Chrumko has money, he can buy a cereal bar right away without finding someone who wants exactly an apple. Money makes it simpler.

questions.question: Imagine you want to buy bread but money didn't exist. What would you have to do?
options: You could get bread without anything
You would have to offer the baker something in exchange that the baker would want
The baker would give you bread for free
You couldn't buy bread at all
questions.explanation: Without money, you would have to trade bread for something the baker likes and would accept. That's harder than simply paying with money.

lessons.lessonName: How people paid in the past

questions.question: What was the name of the exchange of items when money didn't exist?
questions.explanation: Before money was created, people used direct exchange called barter - direct exchange of goods for goods.

questions.question: Chrumko wants bread from the baker and the baker asks for two eggs. What must Chrumko do?
options: Nothing, because the baker is willing to buy
He can buy bread right away
questions.explanation: If Chrumko doesn't have eggs, he has to get them first. That's why payments were more complicated in the past.

questions.question: What items did ancient cultures use as money?
options: Salt, shells, or metal - things that had value for many people
questions.explanation: Later, people paid with things that had value for many, such as salt, shells, or metal. Only then did the first coins appear.

questions.question: Why was payment with salt easier than direct barter?
options: Because everyone wanted salt and could use it to buy various things
questions.explanation: People needed salt, so everyone accepted it as payment. That was easier than direct barter because salt had value for many people.

questions.question: How many forms do money have?
options: Three - coins, banknotes, and digital money
questions.explanation: Money can have different forms: we hold coins and banknotes in our hand, digital money is stored in an account and we pay with a card or mobile phone.

questions.question: How does cash work?
options: We pay with banknotes and coins that we hold in our hand
We use only a credit card for this
questions.explanation: If we pay with banknotes and coins, we use cash - money that we keep in our hand or wallet.

questions.question: Chrumko wants to buy a tie. The sales assistant offers him two options. Which is card payment?
questions.explanation: When he pays with a card, money is sent digitally from the account. If he pays with banknotes and coins, he uses cash. Both mean paying with money, just differently.

questions.question: What is digital money?
options: Money stored in an account that we pay with by card or mobile phone
questions.explanation: Digital money is stored in an account and we pay with it using a card or mobile phone. It's not physical, but it has real value.

questions.question: Does a coin with the number 50 have the same value as a banknote with the number 50?
options: No, a coin with 50 has less value because 50 cents is less than 50 euros
A coin is always more expensive
Numbers have nothing to do with it
questions.explanation: Not all money has the same value. A coin with the number 50 has less value than a banknote with the number 50 because 50 cents is less than 50 euros.

questions.question: Chrumko has one euro in his wallet. Juice costs 90 cents and a biscuit costs 50 cents. What can he buy?
options: He can buy only one - either juice or a biscuit
questions.explanation: Juice (90 cents) + biscuit (50 cents) = 140 cents = 1.40 euros. That's more than 1 euro, so Chrumko can't buy both. He has to choose.

questions.question: How do you know how much money you have if you have several coins and banknotes?
options: Know the value of each coin and banknote and add them up
Each banknote is always ten coins
questions.explanation: When we know the value of coins and banknotes, we can count how much money we have and what we can buy with it.

questions.question: If Chrumko had more money, what could he do?
options: He can buy everything in the whole store
He could buy both things - juice and a biscuit - at once
questions.explanation: If Chrumko had more money, say 1.50 euros, he could buy everything he wanted - both juice and a biscuit.

questions.question: What happens when you spend all your money at once?
options: You can't buy anything else with it
questions.explanation: When we spend money, we can't buy anything else with it. That's why it's important to think about what we use it for.

questions.question: Chrumko gets 5 euros and buys candy for 5 euros. What happens?
options: He spent all the money, so he can't buy a new toy
questions.explanation: Chrumko buys candy for 5 euros and then can't buy a new toy. He spent all his money at once, so nothing is left.

questions.question: What should Chrumko do next time?
options: Spend everything at once like last time
Set aside part of the money so he has money for other things he will want later
questions.explanation: Next time, Chrumko should set aside part of the money so he has money for other things he will want later. That's a smart approach.

questions.question: Why is it important to think about how we use money?
options: Because we have only a certain amount of money and when we spend it, we can't buy anything else
questions.explanation: Everyone has only a certain amount of money. When we spend it, we can't buy anything else. That's why it's important to think about what we use it for.

questions.question: How do people most often get money?
options: They find it on the street
They get it for work - salary or wage
questions.explanation: People most often get money for work. When an adult works, they get a reward for their work called salary or wage.

questions.question: How does money get into a family these days?
options: It comes electronically to a bank account
questions.explanation: Money these days often doesn't come in cash, but is deposited into a bank account.

questions.question: What is the money used for that the family gets for work?
options: For housing, food, clothing, transportation, and other things
questions.explanation: From this money, the family pays for housing, food, clothing, transportation, and other things needed for the household to function.

questions.question: How do children most often get money?
options: They get pocket money or money as a gift, for example on birthdays
questions.explanation: Children usually don't get money from work like adults. They might get pocket money or money as a gift, for example on their birthday.

questions.question: What are needs?
options: Things without which our body and daily life would not function properly
questions.explanation: Needs are things without which our body and daily life would not function properly - food, water, clothing, and a safe place to live.

questions.question: Why do we need food and water?
options: They give us energy and help our body stay healthy
questions.explanation: Food and water give us energy and help our body stay healthy. These are basic needs that we need regularly.

questions.question: After school, Chrumko goes to the store. What does he most likely buy first?
options: A snack (food) because he knows he needs food
questions.explanation: Chrumko goes to buy a snack first because he knows he needs food. Only then does he think about whether he has money left for chocolate.

questions.question: How does clothing protect us?
options: It protects us from cold, heat, or rain
questions.explanation: Clothing protects us from cold, heat, or rain. Housing gives us security and a place to rest.

questions.question: What are wants?
options: Things we want but are not necessary for life
questions.explanation: Wants are things we want but are not necessary for life. We can live without them, but they make us happy or entertained.

questions.question: Chrumko comes home hungry. Does he play video games first or eat?
options: He eats because he knows his body needs food
questions.explanation: Chrumko eats first because he knows his body needs food. After eating, he can enjoy his games.

questions.question: What does Chrumko understand about needs?
options: Needs must be satisfied first, then we can think about wants
questions.explanation: Chrumko understands that needs must be satisfied first. Only when we have food, clothing, and shelter can we think about other things.

questions.question: Is it bad to have wants?
options: No, it's natural, but we have to prioritize needs first
Yes, we should never want anything
questions.explanation: It's not bad to have wants. It's natural to want things. But we must first make sure we have everything we need.
